40414938.body_region: brain ventricular system and cerebrospinal fluid (neonatal)
40414938.clinical_problem: Whether sex-related differences and their genetic correlates exist in the neonatal brain ventricular system and cerebrospinal fluid, as measured by automated MRI segmentation.
40414938.patient_population: 75 full-term neonates (44 male, 31 female; gestational age 37-42 weeks) without significant MRI abnormalities, from the dHCP database
40414938.model_description: Deep-learning automated segmentation of brain MRI was used to measure volumes of the lateral ventricles, third ventricle, choroid plexus, and CSF spaces in neonates; the measurements were then related to sex, postnatal age, and gene expression by linear/LASSO regression (not part of the imaging model itself).
40414938.study_design: retrospective observational study using automated MRI segmentation, dHCP cohort

40425959.clinical_problem: Automatic segmentation of diffuse midline glioma (DMG) on multimodal brain MRI to support tumor assessment in this rare, poor-prognosis pediatric brainstem cancer.
40425959.patient_population: 52 pediatric patients with diffuse midline glioma (H3 K27M-altered), 70 MRI studies
40425959.model_description: A modified 3D U-Net with residual blocks takes T1-weighted and T2-weighted/FLAIR MRI (individually or combined) as input and outputs a segmentation mask of the DMG tumor.
40425959.headline_result: Average Dice Similarity Coefficient of 0.883 on the test dataset (best with combined T1W + T2W/FLAIR)
40425959.study_design: retrospective model development and internal test-set evaluation

40437331.body_region: fetal anatomy (brain, femur, thorax, cervix, abdomen)
40437331.clinical_problem: Automated classification of fetal ultrasound standard planes to assist obstetricians in identifying relevant fetal anatomy.
40437331.patient_population: Largest benchmark fetal ultrasound plane dataset (patient count not stated)
40437331.model_description: A lightweight EfficientNet-based CNN with an attention mechanism and 3-layer perceptron classifies fetal ultrasound images into standard anatomical planes (brain, femur, thorax, cervix, abdomen), with GradCAM used to visualize the regions driving each prediction.
40437331.dataset_size: largest benchmark fetal-plane ultrasound dataset (size not stated in abstract)
40437331.headline_result: Top-1 accuracy 96.25%, Top-2 accuracy 99.80%, F1-score 0.9576, with 40x fewer parameters than benchmark models
40437331.study_design: retrospective model development and evaluation on a public benchmark dataset

40441215.clinical_problem: Automated 3D segmentation of vertebrae on CT to support surgical planning in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
40441215.model_description: U-Net and Attention U-Net take 3D CT images of the spine as input and output vertebral segmentation masks, evaluated against ground-truth annotations by Dice coefficient and Hausdorff distance.
40441215.dataset_size: 31 AIS patients, high-resolution CT covering cervical to lumbar spine
40441215.headline_result: U-Net Dice 92.2 ± 2.4% (HD 9.80 ± 1.34 mm); Attention U-Net Dice 92.3 ± 2.9% (HD 8.67 ± 3.38 mm), with Attention U-Net significantly better HD in mid-thoracic scoliosis sites (P = .027)
40441215.study_design: retrospective model development and comparison study

40454500.model_name: RNN-AHF (Rough Neural Network and Anti-Homomorphic Filter)
40454500.clinical_problem: Enhancing and classifying hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) lesions on neonatal brain MRI, which are diffuse, small, and low-contrast and therefore hard to stage.
40454500.patient_population: Neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (sample size not stated)
40454500.model_description: The RNN-AHF framework takes neonatal brain MRI as input, reduces pixel dimensionality and removes artifact-related noise, then enhances and classifies the HIE lesion region using an anti-homomorphic filter combined with a rough neural network.
40454500.headline_result: Lesion image enhancement and classification accuracy of approximately 93.5%

40472424.model_family: transformer (Vision Transformer) with multi-feature fusion / YOLOv8
40472424.clinical_problem: Improving the accuracy and ease of assessing fetal head flexion (occiput-spine angle) during labor, which is technically difficult for less experienced ultrasound operators.
40472424.patient_population: 1,688 posterior mid-sagittal fetal ultrasound images (occiput-spine angle dataset)
40472424.model_description: OSAM-NET uses YOLOv8 to localize the fetal occiput and spine on ultrasound and a Vision Transformer to extract global image features, fusing the geometric and global information via multi-head self-attention to output a predicted occiput-spine angle for assessing fetal head flexion.
40472424.headline_result: R² improved by nearly 13% over comparison models; intraclass correlation coefficient averaged 0.89 versus ultrasound experts; validated on a prospective test dataset
40472424.study_design: model development with prospective test-set validation

40472589.exclusion_reason: EEG-based ictal-fear localization study in children; no imaging AI, EEG signals only.

40481978.model_family: logistic regression and voting classifier ensemble (radiomics)
40481978.clinical_problem: Predicting pathological subtype of peripheral neuroblastic tumors non-invasively from 123I-MIBG SPECT/CT imaging, to help guide treatment planning and surgical decisions.
40481978.patient_population: 67 pediatric patients with peripheral neuroblastic tumors
40481978.model_description: Radiomic features (1702 extracted) from 123I-MIBG SPECT/CT images are combined with clinical features and fed into a logistic regression model and a four-algorithm voting classifier to predict the pathological subtype of peripheral neuroblastic tumors.
40481978.dataset_size: 67 pediatric patients (1702 radiomic features extracted, 7:3 train/validation split)
40481978.headline_result: Voting classifier: macro-average AUC 0.968 (training), 0.879 (test); combined clinical+radiomic logistic regression model: macro-average AUC 0.871 (training), 0.836 (test)

40500925.clinical_problem: Screening for scoliosis and, further, for atypical scoliosis patterns associated with Chiari Malformation type I using spinal X-rays.
40500925.patient_population: 508 pairs of coronal/sagittal spinal radiographs from patients with Chiari-malformation-associated scoliosis, adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, and normal controls
40500925.model_description: Several ResNet-50-based fine-grained classification models (Coronal, Sagittal, Dual, Concat, Bilinear variants) take coronal and/or sagittal spine radiographs as input and output a scoliosis diagnosis and, for scoliotic cases, a classification distinguishing atypical (Chiari-malformation-associated) from typical adolescent idiopathic scoliosis; heatmaps highlight the radiographic features driving classification.
40500925.dataset_size: 508 pairs of coronal and sagittal spinal radiographs
40500925.headline_result: ResNet-50 Dual model reached the diagnostic level of senior spine surgeons for CMS diagnosis; ResNet-50 Coronal model surpassed senior surgeons in specificity and PPV

40507257.model_description: A brief letter/comment responding to a published review, 'Artificial Intelligence for Neuroimaging in Pediatric Cancer' (Dalboni da Rocha et al., Cancers 2025), discussing that review's coverage of AI applications in pediatric cancer neuroimaging.
40507257.study_design: letter / commentary on a published review

40527225.exclusion_reason: AI-ECG (electrocardiogram) model, not radiologic imaging; study population predominantly adult/adolescent >16 years.

40541073.model_name: MRANet and MLRANet (Multiple [Large] Receptive Attention Network)
40541073.clinical_problem: Differentiating incomplete Kawasaki disease from pneumonia and other febrile illnesses via echocardiographic detection of coronary artery abnormalities, particularly where pediatric cardiologists are unavailable.
40541073.patient_population: 203 echocardiographic studies (pediatric patients with suspected incomplete Kawasaki disease vs. pneumonia/other febrile illness)
40541073.model_description: MRANet and MLRANet use multiple (large) receptive attention layers on echocardiographic images/video to detect coronary artery abnormalities and distinguish incomplete Kawasaki disease from pneumonia, aiming to match expert pediatric cardiologist performance.
40541073.headline_result: MLRANet: sensitivity 93.48%, specificity 66.15% for coronary artery abnormality detection, exceeding expert-level performance
40541073.study_design: retrospective model development and comparison study

40541757.exclusion_reason: Adult midlife cohort (mean age 53.6) fMRI study; childhood cardiovascular risk only assessed retrospectively as a covariate, not imaged in children.

40550405.clinical_problem: Generating high-resolution infant brain MRI from low-resolution scans to reduce long acquisition times that are hard for infants to tolerate.
40550405.model_description: An unsupervised single-image super-resolution model, trained using only one low-resolution image plus k-space consistency and self-supervised learning (no paired high-resolution training data required), takes a low-resolution infant brain MRI as input and outputs a higher-resolution reconstruction.
40550405.study_design: methods development study with quantitative and qualitative image-quality evaluation

40551697.exclusion_reason: General ACL anatomy review across all ages; AI/deep learning mentioned only in passing, not the focus and not pediatric-specific.

40561752.exclusion_reason: Retinal OCT study in pediatric OCD; non-radiologic imaging (retina/OCT), excluded modality.

40562012.clinical_problem: Using connectomic mapping to guide surgical planning for pediatric cerebral arteriovenous malformations by visualizing white matter tracts near the lesion.
40562012.patient_population: 2 pediatric patients (9-year-old and 8-year-old females) with cerebral AVM
40562012.model_description: A machine learning algorithm generates patient-specific reconstructions of white matter tracts (corticospinal tract, optic radiations) and functional networks (default mode, language) from anatomic and diffusion tensor MRI, overlaid on intraoperative neuronavigation to guide surgical corridor selection and risk assessment.
40562012.headline_result: Both patients had favorable neurologic outcomes at available follow-up

40564625.model_family: KNN, gradient boosting machine (GBM), random forest, logistic regression (radiomics ensemble)
40564625.clinical_problem: Predicting which children with posterior fossa tumors will develop cerebellar mutism syndrome after surgery, using presurgical imaging.
40564625.patient_population: 247 pediatric patients with posterior fossa tumors (training n=174, validation n=73), mean age 4.88 years
40564625.model_description: Presurgical MRI is used to extract radiomic and lesion-location (voxel distribution) features, which are combined with clinical variables (gender, tumor location, weight) and fed into KNN, GBM, random forest, and logistic regression models to predict postoperative cerebellar mutism syndrome.
40564625.dataset_size: 247 pediatric patients (174 training, 73 validation), Beijing Children's Hospital
40564625.study_design: retrospective model development and validation study

40572652.exclusion_reason: Prediction model built on maternal metabolic/inflammatory biomarkers (XGBoost); fetal aortic wall thickness is an outcome measurement, not an image analyzed by AI.

40576676.model_family: PCA-FFNN (Principal Component Analysis + Feedforward Neural Network)
40576676.clinical_problem: Noninvasively predicting the Sella turcica reference point for aligning 3D cranial stereophotographs in infants with craniosynostosis, to avoid the radiation of repeated CT for cranial morphology assessment.
40576676.model_description: A PCA-FFNN model takes 3D cranial surface models (derived from CT/stereophotography) as input and predicts the Sella turcica coordinate, used to align 3D stereophotographs within a standardized reference frame as a noninvasive alternative to CT-based cranial assessment.
40576676.headline_result: PCA-FFNN achieved significantly lower Sella turcica coordinate prediction error than the conventional CCFP method (3.61 vs. 8.38 mm, P < 0.001)
40576676.study_design: retrospective model development and comparison study

40581397.exclusion_reason: General review of bilingual reading-brain development; no imaging AI model.

40602598.clinical_problem: Whether children with elevated ADHD symptoms have structural brain differences in regions related to mathematical ability, distinguishing general (executive function) versus specific (calculation) deficits.
40602598.patient_population: Children with ADHD symptoms and matched controls from a public pediatric brain-imaging dataset of mathematical development
40602598.model_description: Radiomics features (including shape features) are extracted from structural brain MRI in children with and without elevated ADHD symptoms to identify brain regions associated with mathematical performance, using a public dataset of mathematical brain development.
40602598.study_design: retrospective case-control radiomics study using a public dataset

40612472.exclusion_reason: Mammography report NLP dataset from adult patients; not pediatric.

40621150.exclusion_reason: Dental caries detection on dental radiographs; excluded non-radiologic (dental) imaging.

40628455.exclusion_reason: Survey of an AI-education workshop for pediatric surgeons; no imaging AI model developed or evaluated.

40643671.model_family: deep learning (keypoint detection + segmentation + classification pipeline)
40643671.clinical_problem: Automating Lenke classification of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis from spinal radiographs to assist spinal surgeons.
40643671.patient_population: 860 spinal radiographs from 215 AIS patients (4 views) plus 1220 radiographs from 610 patients (AP and lateral views only)
40643671.model_description: The model performs keypoint detection and pedicle segmentation on spinal radiographs, then applies a custom classification strategy to automatically assign the Lenke curve type, lumbar modifier, and thoracic sagittal profile for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
40643671.dataset_size: 860 radiographs from 215 patients (161 training/54 testing) plus 1220 radiographs from 610 patients
40643671.headline_result: Mean absolute difference for predicted angles 2.29°; Kappa values 0.866 (curve type), 0.845 (lumbar modifier), 0.827 (thoracic sagittal profile); accuracy 87.07-92.59%
40643671.study_design: retrospective model development and validation study

40652866.exclusion_reason: Case report explicitly states no AI tools were used.

40656458.exclusion_reason: Predictive model uses logistic regression only (conventional statistics); no AI/ML.

40657318.clinical_problem: How well multimodal brain MRI (task fMRI, resting-state fMRI, structural MRI, diffusion tensor imaging) predicts children's cognitive abilities, and how that relationship overlaps with genetic and environmental predictors of mental health.
40657318.patient_population: Children aged 9-10 years from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study
40657318.model_description: Multivariate predictive models take 45 types of brain MRI (task fMRI contrasts, resting-state fMRI, structural MRI, diffusion tensor imaging) as input and output a predicted cognitive-ability score, compared against models based on polygenic scores and environmental factors.
40657318.dataset_size: ABCD Study cohort, children aged 9-10 (n not stated in abstract)
40657318.headline_result: Out-of-sample r = .54 combining all 45 MRI types to predict cognitive abilities (best single modality: 2-Back vs 0-Back fMRI contrast, r = .4); multimodal neuroimaging accounted for 66% of the cognitive ability-mental health relationship
40657318.study_design: cross-sectional predictive modeling study using ABCD Study data (preprint)

40658209.model_family: RTMDet and RTMPose (deep learning landmark detection networks)
40658209.clinical_problem: Automating measurement of adenoid size (and adenoid-nasopharyngeal ratio) on lateral neck/head radiographs to replace labor-intensive manual measurement.
40658209.patient_population: 711 pediatric lateral head and neck radiographs from two centers
40658209.model_description: RTMDet and RTMPose networks detect anatomical landmarks on lateral head/neck radiographs, from which the adenoid size, nasopharynx size, and adenoid-nasopharyngeal ratio (Fujioka's method) are automatically calculated.
40658209.dataset_size: 711 lateral head and neck radiographs from two centers (February-July 2023)
40658209.headline_result: ICC 0.902 for adenoid measurement, 0.868 for nasopharynx, 0.911 for adenoid-nasopharyngeal ratio, versus reference standard

40672806.exclusion_reason: Clinical prediction nomogram using labs, symptoms and one ultrasound score (logistic regression/random forest for feature selection); not an image-analysis AI model.

40677120.exclusion_reason: Retracted article; part of a mass-retraction notice for an unrelated special issue, topic unrelated to pediatric radiology AI.

40678468.model_family: Vision Transformers, Diffusion Models, Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF), graph neural network
40678468.clinical_problem: Improving cardiac motion estimation from echocardiographic image registration, including in fetal echocardiography, to overcome noise, low resolution, and anatomical distortion.
40678468.patient_population: Adult and fetal echocardiography (patients/cases not quantified)
40678468.model_description: An AI architecture combining Vision Transformers, diffusion models, and neural radiance fields, with adversarial/self-supervised contrastive learning and a graph-neural-network anatomical constraint, registers echocardiographic images across cardiac motion to enable real-time motion tracking while preserving heart shape.

40703799.model_family: radiomics with Cox proportional hazards model
40703799.clinical_problem: Improving risk stratification of pediatric medulloblastoma using routine clinical MRI, to allow treatment intensification for high-risk tumors and de-escalation for low-risk tumors.
40703799.patient_population: 119 MRI scans from pediatric medulloblastoma patients across 3 institutions (42, 47, 30 per site)
40703799.model_description: Radiomic features capturing structural deformation, texture, and morphology are extracted from the segmented tumor habitat (edema, enhancing lesion, non-enhancing tumor/cystic core) on MRI and combined via Cox proportional hazards modeling into a RaMP score that stratifies medulloblastoma patients into low- and high-risk survival groups.
40703799.dataset_size: 119 MRI scans from 3 institutions (42, 47, 30 patients per site)
40703799.headline_result: C-indices of 0.7 and 0.63 for risk-group separation when training on Sites 1 and 3 and testing on Site 2 (P = .02, .013)

40718933.exclusion_reason: Retinal/choroidal OCT-angiography study in autism; non-radiologic imaging (retina/OCT), excluded modality.

40721053.clinical_problem: Whether structural connectivity-gray matter covariance coupling differs in children with ADHD and whether this can help classify ADHD.
40721053.patient_population: 109 children with ADHD (age 10.8 ± 2.3) and 105 typically developing controls (age 11.2 ± 2.4)
40721053.model_description: A machine learning pipeline uses structural connectivity-gray matter covariance (SC-GMC) coupling features, derived from diffusion and structural MRI, to classify children as having ADHD or being typically developing.
40721053.dataset_size: 109 children with ADHD, 105 typically developing controls
40721053.headline_result: Classification AUC of 0.67 based on SC-GMC coupling

40722422.exclusion_reason: Fetal growth reference charts built with polynomial/quadratic regression curve fitting; conventional statistics, not a machine-learning diagnostic model.

40737523.exclusion_reason: Qualitative interview/survey study of clinician perceptions of a proposed 3D tool; no imaging cohort or model evaluated, population not clearly pediatric.

40751187.exclusion_reason: ML model predicts renal damage from clinical/lab variables plus a pre-interpreted radiological finding; not a direct image-analysis AI model.

40758204.clinical_problem: Automating bone age and sex assessment from hand-wrist radiographs to support clinical decision-making.
40758204.patient_population: 14,048 hand-wrist radiographs from the 2017 RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge open dataset
40758204.model_description: An InceptionV3-based multi-output model with Squeeze-and-Excitation layers takes a digital hand-wrist radiograph as input and simultaneously outputs a predicted bone age and predicted sex.
40758204.dataset_size: 14,048 hand-wrist radiographs (2017 RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge), 7:2:1 train/val/test split
40758204.headline_result: Bone age: MSE ~25, MAE 3.1, ICC 0.997; sex classification: accuracy 95%, AUC 97%, Cohen's kappa 0.898
40758204.study_design: retrospective model development and internal test-set evaluation using a public dataset

40760174.exclusion_reason: fMRI functional-connectivity study of parental storytelling; no AI/ML method described.

40760627.exclusion_reason: Case report; AlphaFold protein-structure modeling used, not imaging AI.

40761684.model_family: atlas-based and neural network autosegmentation (commercial and in-house AI)
40761684.clinical_problem: Comparing autosegmentation methods for organs at risk in pediatric craniospinal irradiation planning and building a quality-assurance tool to catch autosegmentation errors.
40761684.patient_population: 63 pediatric patients undergoing craniospinal irradiation; QA tool built from 100 CSI patients, tested on 50
40761684.model_description: Atlas-based, commercial AI, and in-house neural network autosegmentation methods take planning CT scans as input and output contours for 13 organs at risk in pediatric craniospinal irradiation; a companion kernel-density-estimation quality-assurance tool flags autosegmentation errors by comparing CT number distributions per organ to a baseline.
40761684.dataset_size: 63 CSI patients for autosegmentation comparison; 100 CSI patients for QA tool baseline, tested on 50 cases
40761684.headline_result: In-house AI outperformed Atlas and commercial AI in overlap and distance metrics (e.g., overlap improvement of 0.01-0.02); QA tool achieved 100% agreement with baseline in 60.7% of in-house AI tests vs ~46% for Atlas/commercial AI
40761684.study_design: retrospective comparison study with a companion QA-tool development

40775990.clinical_problem: Cataloguing the publicly available fetal ultrasound databases that support research and clinical AI development in antenatal care.
40775990.patient_population: Not applicable (review of 14 public fetal ultrasound datasets, 2017-2024)
40775990.model_description: A narrative review analyzing 14 publicly available fetal ultrasound databases (2017-2024), covering their imaging types (2D/dynamic, cardiac video, Doppler, 3D), sample sizes, and technical validation accuracy, to guide future database and AI-model development for fetal ultrasound.
40775990.dataset_size: 14 public fetal ultrasound databases, sample sizes ranging from 25 video sequences to 15,728 images
40775990.headline_result: Technical validation across the reviewed databases/applications showed 82-98% accuracy
40775990.study_design: narrative review of publicly available datasets

40776279.clinical_problem: Improving automatic classification of fetal ultrasound images across pregnancy stages to support clinical workflow.
40776279.patient_population: Fetal/newborn ultrasound images across early, midterm, and newborn stages (sample size not stated)
40776279.model_description: A convolutional neural network (EfficientNet) classifies fetal ultrasound images collected at different pregnancy stages (early, midterm, newborn) into diagnostic categories to support clinical workflow.
40776279.headline_result: EfficientNet showed the best classification performance, particularly at the newborn stage (no numeric accuracy given)

40778164.model_name: CLIF-Net (intersection-guided Cross-view Local- and Image-level Fusion Network)
40778164.clinical_problem: Detecting possible serious bacterial infection (sepsis) in newborns using cranial ultrasound imaging.
40778164.patient_population: 302 cranial ultrasound scans of newborn infants from Mbale Regional Referral Hospital, Uganda
40778164.model_description: CLIF-Net uses two CNN branches with cross-attention-based multi-level fusion to combine coronal and sagittal cranial ultrasound views (exploiting their geometric intersection) and output a classification of possible serious bacterial infection (pSBI) versus non-pSBI in newborns.
40778164.headline_result: CLIF-Net demonstrated substantially enhanced performance over prevailing state-of-the-art infection detection techniques (numeric metrics not given)

40784803.exclusion_reason: Adult patients with decompensated liver cirrhosis; not pediatric.

40785001.clinical_problem: Objectively and quantitatively assessing fetal motor behavior and neurodevelopment from 4D ultrasound video.
40785001.patient_population: 50 four-dimensional ultrasound recordings of normal singleton fetuses, 12-22 gestational weeks
40785001.model_description: A customized DeepLabCut model, trained on manually labeled fetal joint positions, tracks eight fetal joints across 4D ultrasound video frames to quantify joint angular velocity and movement coordination over gestational age.
40785001.headline_result: Model achieved a mean likelihood (tracking accuracy) score of 0.960; inter-rater ICC 0.990, intra-rater ICC 0.961 for manual labeling

40795391.exclusion_reason: ML model (LightGBM) for Kawasaki shock syndrome predicts from laboratory variables (NLR, CD3+%, IL-6); echocardiography included only as report data, not image-analysis AI.

40800743.clinical_problem: Characterizing trial-level intra-individual variability in reaction time (a marker of impaired attention) from functional MRI during a Stop-Signal Task in children.
40800743.patient_population: 8,066 children aged 9-10 years from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study
40800743.model_description: A hidden Markov model is applied to Stop-Signal Task fMRI data to compute, on a trial-by-trial basis, the probability of a child being in a 'good' versus 'poor' attentional state, as one of several methods for modeling intra-individual reaction-time variability and its associated brain activation patterns.
40800743.headline_result: Z-score-based modeling of IIVRT showed the strongest effect sizes in task-related networks (lower IIVRT associated with greater default mode network activation, higher IIVRT with greater dorsal attention network activation)
40800743.study_design: cross-sectional analysis of ABCD Study fMRI data

40804830.exclusion_reason: Conventional semi-quantitative PET metrics (SUV, asymmetry index); no AI/ML algorithm described.

40809396.clinical_problem: Estimating brain white-matter fiber orientation from diffusion MRI in neonates using fewer gradient directions, to enable faster, cheaper scans for identifying neurodevelopmental disorders.
40809396.patient_population: 43 neonatal diffusion MRI datasets from the Developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP)
40809396.model_description: A rotationally equivariant spherical CNN takes reduced-gradient-direction (30% of full protocol) multi-shell diffusion MRI signals from neonates as input and predicts the full Fiber Orientation Distribution (FOD), enabling faster acquisitions while preserving tractography quality.
40809396.headline_result: sCNN significantly outperformed an MLP baseline on MSE, PSNR, angular correlation coefficient, angular error, and peak match rate, with FODs/tractography comparable to a Hybrid-CSD ground truth using only 30% of the full acquisition
40809396.study_design: retrospective methods-development study using dHCP data

40819497.model_family: adversarial domain adaptation network (weakly supervised, GAN-based)
40819497.clinical_problem: Improving skull-stripping (removing non-brain tissue) on newborn brain MRI, which is complicated by the strong domain shift between adult and newborn brain images.
40819497.patient_population: Newborn brain MRI from the Developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP), a private newborn dataset, and synthetic data (patient counts not stated)
40819497.model_description: A weakly supervised adversarial domain-adaptation network, expanded with dHCP data, a private newborn dataset, and GMM-generated synthetic data, takes newborn brain MRI as input and outputs a skull-stripped (brain-only) segmentation mask, generalizing across adult, synthetic, public and private newborn MRI domains.
40819497.headline_result: Dice coefficient 0.9509 ± 0.0055 and Hausdorff distance 3.0883 ± 0.1833 for newborn MRI, surpassing SynthStrip (Dice 0.9412 ± 0.0063, Hausdorff 3.1570 ± 0.1389)

40819875.exclusion_reason: Birth-cohort profile/protocol paper; AI mentioned only as a future research plan, not yet applied.

40824989.clinical_problem: Accurately segmenting the placental contour on ultrasound, which is difficult due to image noise, fuzzy boundaries, and limited clinical resources.
40824989.patient_population: Multiple medical ultrasound datasets (placenta, gestational sac, thyroid nodules); sizes not stated
40824989.model_description: MCBL-UNet, a compact 6-layer U-Net combining Mamba's long-range modeling with CNN local feature extraction, boundary-enhancement, global-context, and attention modules, takes ultrasound images as input and outputs a segmentation mask of the placenta (and gestational sac/thyroid nodules).
40824989.headline_result: MCBL-UNet outperformed 13 existing mainstream segmentation methods on Dice coefficient and mIoU using only 1.31M parameters and 1.26G FLOPs

40831395.exclusion_reason: Retracted article; part of a mass-retraction notice for an unrelated special issue.

40832406.clinical_problem: Whether early life adversity and persistent/recurrent pain have combined effects on brain structure in children, and whether these can be distinguished by structural MRI.
40832406.patient_population: 1,671 children from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study cohort, baseline and 2-year follow-up
40832406.model_description: A support vector machine is applied to structural MRI measures (subcortical volume, cortical thickness, surface area) to classify children into control, persistent/recurrent-pain-only, early-life-adversity-only, and combined-exposure groups.
40832406.headline_result: Support vector machine models classified group status with at best 66.8% accuracy using all brain measures
40832406.study_design: longitudinal normative modelling study using ABCD Study data (preprint)

40838771.exclusion_reason: Retracted article; part of a mass-retraction notice for an unrelated special issue.

40840261.exclusion_reason: General image-augmentation methodology paper tested on mixed adult datasets (chest X-ray, retinal, breast/maternal-fetal ultrasound); not a pediatric-focused study.

40847596.exclusion_reason: EEG-based semantic-processing study in autism; non-imaging (EEG) modality.

40848560.clinical_problem: Automatically detecting dextrocardia (a congenital anomaly) from routine fetal ultrasound sweeps.
40848560.patient_population: 142 pairs of Situs/4CH ultrasound images for training; 14 ultrasound videos (7 normal, 7 dextrocardia) for testing
40848560.model_description: A SegFormer transformer-based model segments fetal chest, spine, stomach, and heart from ultrasound video (Situs and four-chamber views), a quality-assessment module filters uninformative frames, and the relative left/right orientation of stomach and heart is used to classify dextrocardia.
40848560.dataset_size: 142 pairs of Situs/4CH images (training); 14 ultrasound videos, 2,916 frames total (testing)
40848560.headline_result: Dice scores 0.968/0.958/0.953/0.949 for chest/spine/stomach/heart segmentation; dextrocardia classification score (FBCS) of 0.99
40848560.study_design: retrospective model development and internal test-set evaluation

40852408.clinical_problem: Whether binary deep-learning classifiers for pediatric pneumonia subtype (bacterial vs. viral) on chest X-ray are learning genuine pathogen-specific features or 'hallucinating' by relying on generic pneumonia signs.
40852408.patient_population: Pediatric chest X-ray dataset (size not stated)
40852408.model_description: Two binary CNN classifiers (bacterial-vs-normal, viral-vs-normal) and a third bacterial-vs-viral classifier are evaluated on pediatric chest radiographs using Matthews Correlation Coefficient and prediction entropy, to test whether they hallucinate confident but wrong predictions when shown an unseen pneumonia subtype.
40852408.dataset_size: pediatric chest X-ray dataset (size not stated)
40852408.headline_result: Normal/bacterial and normal/viral classifiers consistently and confidently misclassified the unseen pneumonia subtype into their own disease class (hallucination)

40852762.clinical_problem: Whether bladder shape on fluoroscopic imaging is associated with filling pressures and bladder dysfunction in children with spina bifida, and standardizing bladder-shape terminology.
40852762.patient_population: 417 pediatric and adolescent patients with spina bifida who underwent video urodynamics, median age 2.6 years
40852762.model_description: Unsupervised machine-learning cluster analysis is applied to fluoroscopic bladder images from video urodynamics to group bladder shapes objectively, compared against standardized expert classifications (round/oblong/Christmas tree, smooth/trabeculated), and related to bladder filling pressures and dysfunction.
40852762.dataset_size: 417 patients (fluoroscopic bladder images from video urodynamics)
40852762.headline_result: Clusters with more trabeculated-appearing bladders had statistically significantly higher filling pressures

40853811.clinical_problem: Segmenting the pubic symphysis and fetal head on transperineal ultrasound to calculate the angle of progression, which quantifies fetal head descent during labor, without needing large amounts of manually annotated data.
40853811.patient_population: FH-PS-AoP transperineal ultrasound dataset (size not stated)

40880371.clinical_problem: Characterizing basal ganglia and cerebellar abnormalities in ataxia-telangiectasia (A-T), a condition with under-studied extrapyramidal movement dysfunction, at an individual-patient level.

40880371.model_description: A normative self-supervised deep autoencoder, trained on diffusion (apparent diffusion coefficient) and perfusion (cerebral blood flow) MRI features from healthy children across seven brain regions, reconstructs these features; higher reconstruction error in A-T patients (interpreted via SHAP) identifies abnormal regions at an individual level.

40882812.dataset_size: ABIDE-II public structural MRI dataset (size not stated)
